newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks notch gains, Bombay up for fifth day.
newsitem.headline: India stocks notch gains, Bombay up for fifth day.

text.p: A bout of renewed speculative buying in blue chip stocks aided by an overall buoyant market mood drove major Indian bourses to close at higher levels on Monday, traders said.

"The market trend is a bit confusing. An expected reaction only came from intra-day levels. The mood continues to remain buoyant," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Bombay's Kotak Securities. "People are still looking for a further rally."
Dealers said Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's statement on Monday that the government had no intention as of now to raise prices of petroleum products helped cheer market sentiment.

"As of now, the United Front government has no intention to take such a step," the United News of India quoted the Indian premier as saying in the southern state of Karnataka. He was responding to newspaper speculation about an immediate hike.
Bombay stocks continued their winning streak, closing higher for the fifth consecutive session on Monday after an early fall.
The key 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rebounded from the day's lowest mark of 3,388.80 to finish with a net gain of 34.84 points or 1.02 percent, at 3,453.16.
Some analysts, however, said the rally was likely to peter out in a few days, making way for a much-awaited correction.

"Basically, this is a rally that will not sustain...there is a lot of speculative buying," said Basant Agarwal, equities head at JM Share & Stock Brokers. Foreign funds bought defensive bets like hotels, power, petroleum and pharmaceuticals, he said.
"Prices are going up on expectation of sops offered by the government...We expect the market to see some technical resistance at these levels," Agarwal said.
Dealers said funds were bidders in Cadbury, Brooke Bond and ACC. ITC surged 17.25 rupees to 363.0, SBI 0.25 to 253.75, ACC 58.70 to 1,360.75, Reliance 2.50 to 223.50 and MTNL 7.0 to 256.
